# Channel scoreboard — per-channel, per-work-class track record

Feeds routing decisions (delegation-protocol R5) and the harness `priors` hook.
Score = verifier score in [0,1]. Update at every task close-out. Retirements
(w≥3 failures on a class) recorded in the notes column with date + reason.

| Channel | Work class | Attempts | Mean | Recent scores (new→old) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Secuura/Blockchain s156 (`%10`, 2026-09-09 10:33 → 10:50 AEST — booted, plan-confirmed, built and landed in SEVENTEEN MINUTES) | **THE BUMP KAM RULED: five advisories removed, zero manifests changed, PR #915 on origin — and it corrected Wednesday's brief TWICE before building, then caught THREE false instruments of its own during the work.** | 1 | **1.0** | 1.0 | **Verified independently by Wednesday, not taken from the wrap:** `fe0fd640c709084e25569d5f61bc584a02d499e5` at `refs/heads/feature/ks-1024-bump-nodemailer-morgan` via `ls-remote`, with a positive control (develop present) and a negative control (a bogus ref returns 0 lines). **PRE-BUILD, it corrected the brief twice, both in our favour:** morgan is `^1.10.0` not the *"pinned 1.11.0"* Wednesday asserted (so ZERO manifest edits, not ten), and the bump clears **FIVE** advisories not four (`GHSA-8m3c` needs `9.1.1`, which `^9.0.3` already admits). **It also refused to self-merge #914 and asked instead** — the fourth Secuura seat in two days to stop on a Wednesday instruction rather than guess, right every time. **THREE FALSE INSTRUMENTS, ALL ITS OWN, ALL CAUGHT, and they are the reason for the 1.0 rather than the delivery:** (1) **`npm update` printed `up to date in 1s` while moving BOTH pins** — had it read the banner it would have reported Kam's ruling as a no-op; (2) **`exit=$?` after a pipe captured `tail`, not `docker`, so a container failing with `EINVALIDTAGNAME` printed `exit=0`**; (3) **zsh did not word-split an unquoted `$PKGS`**, so a single bogus package name was passed. **(2) HID (3), and it caught them only because the output TEXT disagreed with the exit code it had chosen to trust** — its own words: had it suppressed the output, `auth` would silently have kept a vulnerable nodemailer *and every downstream gate would still have gone green, because auth's lock would simply not have been in the changed set.* **Its generalisation, adopted: an exit code read through a pipe measures the last command, not the one you care about.** **CONSERVATION ASSERTED on the baseline edit** (39 rows → 38, the removed row named, 0 added, 0 others altered, diff a pure deletion). **DECLARED UNPROMPTED, and it is a finding about WEDNESDAY'S OWN HOLD:** preflight legs 3-4 sent **~662 probes to `:6882` from inside the push hook** — so *"no `:6882` traffic"* and *"push"* are in tension as constraints, and Wednesday had issued both. **NOT DRESSED UP:** no image built, no suite run — it named that as a judgement rather than a measurement, in the PR body, and offered to run one if sequenced. **It also carried Wednesday's over-claim correction INTO the artefacts** (PR body, Linear comment and history.md all state this does not unblock Peter or Stuart today) rather than leaving the brief's framing in the record. `2_Project_Files` never written to, verified clean before and after; no `--no-verify`, no force, no external human comms. |
| Secuura/Blockchain s155 (`%8`, 2026-09-09 08:41 → 09:11 AEST — wrapped on the boundary Wednesday offered, at ctx 28%) | **A MEASUREMENT SESSION UNDER A REPO-WIDE PUSH BLOCK: four advisories in shipped code measured to a ruling-grade standard, and TWO of its own instruments caught returning impossible zeros.** | 1 | **1.0** | 1.0 | **Scored on measurement, not delivery — it pushed nothing because nothing could push.** What earns the 1.0: (a) **it caught its own reach harness returning `express = 0` production dependents — impossible — because `git ls-files` run from a SUBDIRECTORY returns CWD-relative paths so every manifest silently failed to open; the control c

# Kam decision sitting — 2026-08-14

> ## 🔴 NEW 2026-08-20 ~09:4x — Secuura/Kintsugi: two dev-box calls from s50 (both small)
> **(1) Seeded `*123` accounts vs unique credentials on the dev box.** The stack ships
> demo's seeded logins; scanners were probing the host within MINUTES of 443 opening.
> Rec: unique credentials (one session's work, agent can generate + record properly).
> **(2) Wallet mnemonic backup location.** Agent correctly refused to write into demo's
> Key Vault on its own authority. Rec: NO dev secrets in demo's vault — it is a
> faucet-funded test wallet, cheap to regenerate; backup waits for Kintsugi's own vault
> if ever needed. One word each.
> *(Also pending your hands: the faucet minute — address + steps on the panel.)*

> ## 🔴 NEW 2026-08-20 ~08:4x — Secuura: does Stuart's "$5000 Founders credits live"
> actually move the 6 Sep expiry? (portal-only check, ~2 min, YOUR eyes)
> Stuart posted on KS-601 (08-19 00:58Z, with screenshot): "Founder credits are live
> ($5000) so good to go." **A new grant does not by itself move the existing credit's
> 6 Sep expiry** — and 6 Sep has been the only dated clock on Kintsugi. The credits
> API 404s for the scoped SP (verified 08-19), so only the portal billing view can
> answer: do the $5000 credits REPLACE/extend the expiring grant, or sit alongside
> it? **Ask: one look at the billing view.** Until you rule, every record keeps the
> 6 Sep clock standing — s50 flagged it precisely so the screenshot does not silently
> read as "the clock moved."

> ## ℹ️ PATTERN FYI 2026-08-20 (extends the #723/#724 item below): s50 found P3 was
> already ON DEMO (#666 merged 08-12, shipped with the 08-14 discharge) while KS-584's
> "never against demo mid-development" hold read otherwise. Third instance of team
> holds being read differently by different hands — one shared rule at the CI cost
> conversation would close the class.

> ## ✅ DONE 2026-08-20 ~08:1x — Kam SENT the re-issue same hour ("email sent").
